stem: Plants near one end of a room have noticeably longer internodes than plants elsewhere. What should a Technician I do?
choices: Record the location and morphology pattern, compare relevant room conditions or history, and escalate if the pattern is outside expectation
Prune every affected plant before documenting the condition
Ignore the pattern because internode length is never useful
rationale: A spatial morphology pattern is useful evidence. The technician should document it and connect it to available environmental or crop context rather than assigning an unsupported cause.
